_about: The second claim run's analysis, fixed on 22 October 2026 before any of its data exists, as the first claim's was before its run: docs/content/claim2-protocol.md, 'Arms' and 'Measures and analysis'. Read by claim.py --protocol experiments/tasks/claim2_analysis.json <the claim command's manifest>.

arms: each protocol arm by what its batches' payloads record, the retrieval instruction suite.arm_of names and the scripted user's reading under the box, with the suite flags that make it. Every arm runs with --max-steps 300 --clock 1800, which 'require' holds the runs to.

sets: question ids of the claim market's task file, which env/generate_aplus_tasks.py --rewordings writes. 'held_out' is no list: it is every task of that file with a 'template', the meaning-kept rewordings of experiments/tasks/paraphrases_v2.json, read by id and template only. Superseded in part in version 7: the held-out rewordings are v2's tee entries and the v3 set, and a set may select among them by a field of their task.

tests: the four primary tests, two-sided, Holm over the four. H1 and H4 are stratified exact tests of correct, by question and by template; H2 and H3 van Elteren's stratified exact rank test, by question, and H3 is reported on the agent's tokens beside its cost, outside Holm (the model parser's tokens are not recorded, its charge is in the cost). Superseded in part: since cce9ab0 (23 October 2026) the parse's tokens are recorded, and a run's tokens, which H3 reports, include them.

design: the questions each arm asks, every round. 'templates' are the market's fifteen questions; the rewordings are asked under the block alone, since only H4 reads them. The number of rounds is the protocol's to fix from the dry run's estimate. Superseded: since version 6 the design is one for each model, and each set an arm asks has rounds of its own; since version 7 the templates are the market's thirteen.

models: each its own result, never pooled. The ids are those the runs record (MODEL_NAME); a model the runs record that is not named here is analysed and said to be unnamed, and a model named here with no run is a problem.
Version 2, 23 October 2026, from the verifier's fairness audit, before any run 2 data exists:

roles: DeepSeek's four tests are the primary result and the claim, with Holm over its four. Haiku's four are a replication of it, a family of their own with their own Holm over four; the two are never pooled and neither corrects the other. Superseded in part: since version 6 Haiku's family is H1 alone, with Holm over that one test; since version 7 Haiku runs no arm in the shop (decision 6 of 24 October 2026) and is in the reading test alone, so DeepSeek is the one model named.

H2 and H3 count only the slots where the agent ran. A slot the box closes, an ask with no reply or a decline, runs no agent, and entered H2 and H3 as 0 listings and the parse's cost; only the block under the model closes such slots on the gated questions, so it could only favour the model. The closed slots are left out and reported beside each test by question and arm, and the sensitivity 'with the closed slots in H2 and H3' puts them back.

Every run's sorting and page size are counted from its log, by arm: product_list_order or product_list_dir in an address its navigations asked for or its replies reported is a sort (relevance, the default, is none), product_list_limit or the list view is a change of page size (experiments/analysis/toolbar.py). The page rules hold for the relevance order at 36 a page only; at 60 a page all 42 listings render on one. The sensitivity 'without the runs that sorted or changed the page size' drops them. Superseded in part in version 7: design B's market has about 45 listings, and at 60 a page every one of them renders on one page all the same.

H4 stays one test of all thirteen keyed templates. splits: H4 again on each part of two pre-specified splits, secondary and unadjusted: the first claim's six templates against the seven added for the second, and the tee's eight against the water's five. Both parsers are deterministic, so the box makes one plan of a rewording whatever the round, and the unit at the front door is the 26 keyed rewordings, not the runs: the sensitivity 'H4 by rewording, not by run' takes each rewording's share of its runs correct, one value a rewording and arm, van Elteren's stratified exact rank test by template. Superseded in part in version 7: H4 is one test of the ten keyed templates, and its two splits are design B's, below.

failure_breakdown: the shipped arm's runs on the gated questions that a key judged not correct, each coded by the first of these written rules that holds. 'page 2 never reached': no address the run's navigations asked for or its replies reported is a results page numbered 2 or more, or one whose product_list_limit exceeds the page size, 36; on this market both products have listings on page 2 (env/generate_aplus.py, rule interleaved). 'a card or sold-out price taken': the answer states a listing's advertised price, or the price of the question's size or pack at a listing where it is sold out, among the listings of the question's product in the fixture the shop was seeded from, that the key does not hold as right. 'other': anything else.
Version 3, 23 October 2026, from the verifier's re-audit of version 2 (dede8fe), before any run 2 data exists:

require: every arm is held to the step budget, the clock and the pinned browser tool, and each arm to its own conditions under arms.<name>.require: open everything to the product wording's version; each block arm to the box's version, its page reader, its rate plan and every other version a box batch records, so the two arms H4 compares run the same front door but for the parser; the model arm also to the parser's prompt, temperature and normalisation. claim.py refuses the batches when any run records another (R4); until version 3 only the step budget and the clock were required, and a batch under another was listed and analysed all the same. tests/test_claim2_analysis.py holds each required version to the code's own constant.

Pending the student's decision on the evening of 23 October 2026: both block arms run with --reading own, the scripted user answering each question with the reading its own key was written under (suite.scripted_reply), and --rate-plan every, a rate question planned over every listing with no bound. If either is not chosen, the arm's flags, its reading and its require change with it, before any run. Decided (decision 8 of 24 October 2026): --reading own; the rate plan is superseded in version 7, below.
H3's tokens include the model parser's since 23 October 2026 (suite.charge_parse, claim.stated_tokens), as its charge always was in the cost.

failure_breakdown is on the reading-independent questions, H1's (R5), and 'page 2 never reached' codes a failure only where the question's key needs a listing past the first results page, by where its listings render in the market's results order (claim.needs_a_later_page): for a price, a best, a ranking or a count any one of them past it, for a yes or a no every one. On the other questions a run that read only the first page is coded by the rules after it.

The sensitivity 'with the closed slots in H2 and H3 at open everything's median' puts each closed slot back at open everything's median listings and cost for its question, as if each had run as open everything runs (R6), a cautious value where the agent ran nothing; 'with the closed slots in H2 and H3' stays.

secondary_measures: the asks, the box's or the agent's own, on the questions the sidecar labels clear and on those it labels ambiguous (its two_readings), as a share of runs with Wilson's 95% interval, by arm and model; and who served each run's model calls, from its log, by arm, with H3 within each provider that served whole runs of both its arms where the arms' mixes differ (R11), unadjusted.

claim.py --sheet writes every answer counted as a blind hand-reading sheet, each under a random code in place of its arm, model and run, and the key that maps the codes back, in case the hand reading is chosen as a sensitivity. Superseded in part: answers to a question with no key (protocol analysis v5) and runs with no key for the reading they were answered under (v7), which are unscored, are left off the sheet, each counted in its key file, as docs/content/claim2-reading-rules.md says; and since version 7 the hand reading is the verdict of record (decision 5 of 24 October 2026), with the second reader's sample drawn by the rule under hand_reading.
Version 4, 23 October 2026, from the auditor's check of version 3 (41d7839), before any run 2 data exists:

A batch outside require is void as a whole, re-run, and listed. claim.py leaves it out of every figure and lists it with the conditions it ran under; a model it leaves a slot empty for, not run again, is refused, and the other model's analysis is not touched. Its charges still count among the money spent.

require: every arm is also held to the agent's code, the agent-core submodule's commit and the digest of agent/openjiuwen-local.patch (suite.agent_code_identity), and to the browser's origins and flags (suite.browser_conditions). The model arm's parser_model is held to the run's own model ({"same_as": "model"}).

The claim command checks each invocation before it runs: claim.py --protocol experiments/tasks/claim2_analysis.json --preflight <arm> --flags "<the suite.py flags>" works out what the batch would record under the code as it stands and exits 1 on any condition outside require, spending nothing.

secondary_measures adds the parse's fallbacks by arm and model, from each run's box record: the survey fallback (its 'fallback', a shopping question no shape fits) and, under the model parser, the rules' form used and why (its parse's 'fallback_reason').

failure_breakdown: a shipped run that sorted the results or changed their page size and read its own first page alone is coded 'sorted or resized, its first page alone', never 'page 2 never reached', since where a key's listings render holds for the relevance order at 36 a page only. env/check_aplus_market.py checks the live order against the order claim.py reads where the listings render, the one the seed search recorded when it accepted the market, as well as against the predicted one.
Version 5, 23 October 2026, the freeze candidate with OpenRouter provider routing (IGR_PROVIDER_ROUTING, experiments/runners/provider_routing.py), before any run 2 data exists:

provider_routing: the OpenRouter provider object every call of a model's arms carries, the agent's and, in the arm the model parser reads, the parse's; null is off. Every arm of a model is held to it: a batch whose payload's provider_routing, or a run whose record's, is not it is outside require, void as a whole, and so is a run whose record's routing is not the one its batch's payload says the agent ran under. claim.py --preflight reads IGR_PROVIDER_ROUTING from the environment and refuses an invocation it would route otherwise.

Pending decision 9 on the evening of 23 October 2026: DeepSeek V4 Flash routed to gmicloud, deepinfra and streamlake in that order with no fallback, and at fp8 alone ("quantizations": ["fp8"], since the verifier's check of 281c7e8, so an endpoint that changes its quantisation is not used either), the value provider_routing.PROPOSED holds, and Haiku off. If routing is not chosen, 'off' means null for DeepSeek too, and the batches are run with IGR_PROVIDER_ROUTING unset. A provider object's keys are held to OpenRouter's documented ones (provider_routing.PROVIDER_KEYS): a typo is refused, by suite.py, the preflight and this file's check alike, where OpenRouter would ignore it. Decided (decision 7 of 24 October 2026): DeepSeek is routed so, for every arm alike.

The serving-provider mix by arm and model is read from each row's count of who served the agent's calls and from its parse_provider, a batch from before routing by the same reading of its logs, and a run whose count is missing is unknown, never zero.

The hand reading (claim.py --sheet, then --hand): a reader marks an answer 'unscorable' only when it cannot be read at all, being empty, garbled, or about another question; any answer that can be read is 'correct' or 'not correct' against its key, however hedged or long. An unscorable answer leaves every test of correct, so --hand counts them by arm and model and prints, beside each test of correct, how many it leaves out.
Version 6, 23 October 2026, for the student's decision 2 (the budget), before any run 2 data exists:

design: one for each model, and each set an arm asks in rounds of its own: 'asks' gives each arm the model runs its sets ('templates' or a set named under 'sets') with the rounds each is asked in, and 'tests' the family the model holds, with its own Holm over that family. The primary model's family holds every test. An arm, test, comparison or sensitivity a model's design leaves out is reported as not run by design, never as missing data or a refusal; a run the design does not ask for is listed among the problems and is in no figure, so each test, H4 and its sensitivities included, reads only the rounds its design has. A test's two arms are asked its questions in the same rounds, which claim.py holds the file to.

Pending decision 2 on the evening of 23 October 2026, the file holds plan 2a: DeepSeek runs the full design, the templates in rounds 1 to 3 under all four arms and the held-out rewordings in round 1 alone under both block arms, so H4 has one run a rewording an arm; Haiku runs only shipped and the block (model), on the nine reading-independent questions, in round 1 alone, and its family is H1 alone, with Holm over that one test. Plan 2b is 2a with the held-out rewordings in rounds [1, 2, 3]; plan 2c is 2a with every set of DeepSeek's in rounds [1, 2]. If either is chosen, the rounds here change with it, before any run. Decided (decisions 6 and 13 of 24 October 2026): plan 2a's rounds for DeepSeek, and no Haiku arm in the shop.

Version 7, 24 October 2026, design B, the tee-only market with misleading size labels (docs/content/claim2-handover.md, the student's decisions of 00:30 to 01:35 and the verifier's question check), before any run 2 data exists:

The market is one product, a tee, under one brand, about 45 listings from distinct sellers over two results pages at 36 a page, sizes XS to XXL, each absent, sold out or buyable at its own price; promo labels on size XS alone, every one false, the figure at least 8% below the real XS price; scarcity labels on buyable size M alone; no description. So there is no water question, no per-litre question and no multipack hint: a question whose difficulty is arithmetic, not retrieval, is out (decision 2).

sets: 'control' tee-headline; 'decline' the three the block should not plan, decline-delivery, decline-fit and decline-scarcity, keyless; 'gated' the eight keyed questions open everything asks, every keyed template but tee-headline and tee-promo-check, since open everything on one named listing is meaningless; 'lookup' tee-promo-check, the check of a named listing's label, which only shipped and the block arms ask; 'two_readings' tee-all-stocked and tee-count-stocked, their own key the menu reading and a buyable key in the sidecar; 'reading_independent' the seven keyed questions with one reading that H1 and the failure breakdown read, tee-promo-check among them though it is outside 'gated', which the protocol loader allows (the first claim's refused it); 'held_out' every task with a template; 'held_out_v2' and 'held_out_v3' the held-out rewordings by the file their task says it came from, its 'source' (env/generate_aplus_tasks.py, fixed with its coder); 'kept_templates' the eight tee templates kept word for word from the A+ design, 'new_templates' tee-xs-price and tee-promo-check; 'promo_trap' the two questions the promo labels are a trap on.

arms: the four as before, every one with --max-steps 300 --clock 1800, the block arms with --reading own and --page-reader rendered. --rate-plan every is dropped, with its requirement: the rate plan changes a plan only on a rate question, one asked per litre (primitives.every_rate, a form of kind rate_bound), and design B asks none, so the flag was inert; the batch records the default, 'bound', which require holds every block batch to, so two rate plans are still never pooled.

models: DeepSeek V4 Flash alone in the shop, the primary, Holm over H1 to H4. Claude Haiku 4.5 runs no arm: it is in the text-only reading test alone, named under reading_test, descriptive, with no family and no Holm. A Haiku batch in the shop would be a model this file does not name, analysed apart and listed.
design: DeepSeek asks the templates in rounds 1 to 3 under all four arms (open everything the gated set), and the held-out rewordings in round 1 under both block arms, as plan 2a had it.

splits of H4, both pre-specified, secondary and unadjusted, each within a set: 'v2 against v3' within the kept eight templates, since v2 has no entry for the new templates; and 'the two new templates against the kept eight' within v3 alone. A split's parts are two sets of templates or two sets of rewordings, disjoint, that together cover the test's questions within the restriction (claim.split_scope), or the file is refused. No other split, and the sensitivity 'H4 by rewording, not by run' stays.

against_open_everything stays on the reading-independent questions; tee-promo-check, which open everything does not ask, is reported there as not run by design, by question, never as a row with no runs.

failure_breakdown adds a fifth code, tried after 'a card or sold-out price taken' and before 'other': 'a label's figure taken', the answer states, as a price, a figure a size label shows as a promotion ('XS - Promo $9.99'), read from the fixture's variants whose label_kind is 'promo' (their label_price), among the question's product's listings, that the key does not hold as right and that the question does not itself quote, since tee-promo-check quotes the label's figure to ask whether it holds. The label's figure is no price: the size's price shows once the size is chosen.

secondary_measures adds three, each defined here before any run and each by arm and model. 'asks caused by the word-list clash' (decision 11): of the box's asks, those whose box record gives ask_reason 'clash', the rules' word list and the model having read a word differently, where box v19 asks the shopper instead of taking the rules' form, against 'ambiguous', the question's own two readings; counted by the sidecar's label of the question, clear or ambiguous, every reason the records give listed, and each clash named with whether its ask closed the slot. 'promo traps fallen for, by arm', on the promo_trap set and its rewordings, of the runs where the agent answered, by what the question's key can say: on a price key (tee-xs-price) the run fell for the trap when the price the answer gives as its answer, the one its first claim of a lowest names (score.answer_price) else the first price it states, is a label's promo figure the key does not hold as right, so an answer that names the figure as working and gives the real price has not; on any other key (tee-promo-check) when the answer affirms the label, a yes by the scorer's own yes-or-no reading (score.LEADING_ANSWER, then its markers, the negative first), or says neither yes nor no, states a label's figure and states no price the key holds as right, so an answer that says no has refuted the label whatever price it then gives; a share of the runs that answered, with Wilson's 95% interval, each run named. 'hidden-price leaks by arm': the runs whose log holds a sign of the prices the gated theme hides (experiments/analysis/leaks.py), each named with its first finding. 'declines by arm' and 'sorts and page-size changes by arm' were always computed and are named here so the file says the protocol reports them.

hand_reading: the verdict of record is the student's blind hand reading after the run (decision 5), the scorer reported beside it; the verifier reads a second sample blind, drawn by claim.py --sheet as random.Random(20261024).sample over the sheet's codes in sorted order, 40 rows, written beside the sheet as <name>.second-reader.json, so the sample is the rule's and never a hand's. The agreement of the two readers is computed by a short script committed with the results.

reading_test: after the stage's last block run, each model parses the v2 entries whose template is a tee template or decline-delivery, and every v3 entry, those with template null included, once each as text (parse_probe.py --questions ... --spec-from <the claim task file> --page-from <the stage's first block batch>), DeepSeek routed as in the shop and Haiku unrouted; each form against its template's and each outcome against the entry's expected one, with a v3 entry's ask_kind (availability, threshold, other) held to the ask given, so a 'menu or buyable?' ask on a price word with no figure is not counted right. Descriptive, no test, no family.

The scorer at the freeze is score v10, v8 plus additive kinds (one for tee-promo-check, no plus the real price, and the whole-label blanking so 'M - Only 2 left!' is not read as a count), reported beside the hand reading: a decision taken on the student's behalf at 01:58 on 24 October 2026, pending the generator coder's confirmation. The scorer is no arm's condition: claim.py scores every answer again with the scorer it imports and lists any stored verdict that moves.

require holds the code's constants as they stand at 02:00 on 24 October 2026 (box 18, form 13, prompt 3, normalise 4, primitives 12, targeting 9, planner 2); the box coder bumps the box to 19 and the prompt to 4, and tests/test_claim2_analysis.py holds every required version to the code's own constant, so a gap after the merge fails there before any run.

reading_test.entries: the v2 entries whose template is a tee template or decline-delivery, and every v3 entry, template null included
reading_test.analysis: descriptive: each form against its template's, each outcome against the entry's expected one, a v3 ask held to its ask_kind; no test, no family

codes.rule: the run kept the shop's relevance order at its page size, the question's key needs a listing past the first results page, by where its listings render in the market's results order, and no results page numbered 2 or more, and no product_list_limit above the page size, is among the addresses the run's navigations asked for and its replies reported

codes.code: sorted or resized, its first page alone
codes.rule: the run sorted the results or changed their page size, and no results page numbered 2 or more, and no product_list_limit above the page size, is among the addresses the run's navigations asked for and its replies reported; where a key's listings render holds for the relevance order at the shop's page size only

codes.code: a card or sold-out price taken
codes.rule: the answer states a listing's advertised price, or the price of the question's variant where it is sold out, among the question's product's listings, that the key does not hold as right

the answer states, as a price, a figure a size label shows as a promotion, among the question's product's listings, that the key does not hold as right and that the question does not itself quote; the figure is no price, the size's price shows once it is chosen

hand_reading.verdict_of_record: the student's blind hand reading, score reported beside it

sensitivity: without the runs that saw a hidden price
with the closed slots in H2 and H3
without the runs that sorted or changed the page size
H4 by rewording, not by run
with the closed slots in H2 and H3 at open everything's median
secondary_measures: the serving provider by arm, and H3 by provider
asks caused by the word-list clash
promo traps fallen for, by arm
sorts and page-size changes by arm
